title: A command-line program: arguments, subcommands and output

videos.script: This course is about the Go that runs in production, and most of that Go is a program somebody types into a terminal. So the first lesson builds one. {{lab}} Before any code, the lab. You need the same Go the go course installed, and a C compiler for two lessons much later. Four commands check both, and one section says what to do when they fail. {{args}} Then what a program is given. The shell splits a line into words, and the flag package reads some of those words as settings. The rest are the program's to use. {{commands}} Next, a real tool. It is called hits, and it reads a web server's log and counts what it finds. It has two subcommands, each with flags of its own, built with nothing but the standard library. {{exit}} Last, the contract with whoever runs it. Results go to one stream and complaints to another. The exit code says whether it worked. Get those three right, and your program can sit in a pipeline and in a script. Every later lesson builds on hits.
